content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has published a guideline on the fortification of maize flour and cornmeal with vitamins and minerals. This guideline is intended to provide evidence-based recommendations for the fortification of these staple foods, which are widely consumed in many countries, particularly in Africa and the Americas. The fortification process involves adding essential micronutrients, such as iron, folic acid, B-complex vitamins, vitamin A, and zinc, to address nutritional deficiencies in populations where these foods are dietary staples. The guideline emphasizes that decisions regarding which nutrients to add and in what quantities should be based on the specific nutritional needs and intake gaps of the target population. Other factors to consider include the usual consumption levels of maize flour and cornmeal, the sensory and physical effects of the added nutrients on the food products, the fortification of other food vehicles, the population's use of vitamin and mineral supplements, as well as cost, feasibility, and acceptability. The WHO developed this guideline following rigorous procedures outlined in its handbook for guideline development. The process included identifying priority questions and outcomes, retrieving and assessing evidence, and synthesizing findings to inform recommendations. The guideline is designed to assist Member States and their partners in making informed decisions about nutrition interventions to achieve global health targets, including the Sustainable Development Goals. The document also highlights the importance of industrial fortification of maize flour and cornmeal as a cost-effective and efficient public health strategy. This approach has been practiced for many years in several countries and has been shown to improve the nutritional status of large segments of the population. The guideline complements other WHO and FAO publications on food fortification and provides updated evidence from recent systematic reviews. The WHO acknowledges the contributions of various experts, organizations, and stakeholders involved in the development of this guideline. Financial support for the work was provided by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and other partners. The guideline also benefited from technical input from the Cochrane Public Health Group and other international experts. The recommendations in this guideline supersede previous WHO recommendations on maize flour fortification and are intended for policymakers, technical advisors, and program staff involved in designing and implementing nutrition interventions. The guideline aims to support the development of comprehensive food-based strategies to combat micronutrient deficiencies and improve public health outcomes.
